fields.description:
## Context / Problem

The tickets branch carries a duplicated parallel lineage (investigated on `dissocial-windowy-kusimanse`). Re-measurement replaced the earlier "stale writer forked the branch" reading: the two lineages pair up commit-for-commit with identical author, author time, committer time, and subject (28,586 matched pairs, zero committer-time differences), differing only in parentage. Independent writers cannot produce that; a filter-repo-style history rewrite does, because it re-creates every descendant commit with its original metadata. The only content difference between the two tips is the small set of event files the rewrite removed.

Root cause: a history rewrite of the tickets branch did not stamp a new store epoch in `.store-compat.json`, and a stale clone that still held the pre-rewrite lineage was later re-merged through `sync._union_merge` ("auto-reconcile during sync"). That merge re-attached the whole pre-rewrite lineage, including the content the rewrite removed.

The store-epoch guard (`mirky-sparse-woodborer`, commit `019e32e03d1`) exists precisely to stop a stale clone resurrecting stripped history, but it only fires when the rewrite stamps a new epoch. Both sides carried the same epoch, so it passed. Nothing in `src/rebar` detects a rewrite that skipped the epoch step, so recurrence is live.

## Approach

Extend the existing guard's purpose with a second, epoch-independent check at the same chokepoint. `compat.store_epoch_merge_target()` is already called by all three union sites before they merge: `sync._union_merge`, and the two push-recovery merges in `push_recovery` (`_merge_remote_under_lock` and the post-stash merge). After the epoch check passes, the same function will refuse the merge when the local-only and remote-only commit sets contain **rewrite copies**:

- Collect non-merge commits in `HEAD ^<pinned target>` and `<pinned target> ^HEAD` with one `git log` each, keyed by (author name, author email, author time, committer name, committer email, committer time, subject).
- For each remote-only commit whose key matches a local-only commit, compare the two commits' changed-path sets (`git diff-tree -r --name-only`). Event filenames embed a UUID, so two genuinely independent commits never share a non-empty path set. Equal non-empty path sets = a copy.
- One confirmed copy refuses the merge with a diagnostic that names the rewrite signature, the count of local-only commits that are NOT copies (work to salvage before re-cloning), and says to re-clone. A git failure while checking fails closed, matching the epoch guard's unreadable-ref behaviour.

The refusal flows through the existing `(target, problem)` return, so every site's established refusal handling (warning, strict-mode error, no merge state left behind, push stays pending, `store fsck` reports DIVERGED) applies unchanged. Ordinary concurrent push-retry merges are unaffected: distinct writes never share a path set, and `cherry-pick`/`rebase` recovery paths rewrite committer time, so their output never keys as a copy.

This is in-process and operation-linked (`project.portability`): it runs inside every union attempt on every host, not in CI. The refusal at merge time is also the detection signal for future rewrite forks; it no longer depends on someone noticing a pack-size step.

Prior evidence, no further action here: the earlier commit-signature sweep found 43 duplicated-event-path cases outside this lineage, clustered on 2026-08-03 across 20 merge-base clusters, which predates the epoch guard (2026-08-04). This ticket does not rewrite or reclaim existing history; leaving the existing duplicate in place is the operator's decision on `dissocial-windowy-kusimanse`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py`: add the rewrite-copy check and call it from `store_epoch_merge_target()` after the epoch check. Stays under 800 lines; no new mechanism (no env var, flag, config key, lock).
- `tests/integration/test_lineage_rewrite_guard.py` (new): real-git sandbox tests, synthetic data only.
- `docs/concurrency.md`: document the rewrite-copy refusal next to the store-epoch refusal.

Out of scope: any change to the live tickets branch, re-redaction, tracker maintenance, or history rewrite.

## Testing

All fixtures are local sandbox repos (bare origin + clones) under `tmp_path`, with synthetic events and fixed `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` dates. The rewrite is simulated filter-repo-style: replay every commit after a dropped one with `git commit-tree` under its original author/committer metadata, then force-push to the sandbox origin. No autouse fixtures; any child process starts with `_subprocess_env.subprocess_env`.

- Stale clone + sync: a clone holding the pre-rewrite lineage runs `sync.reconverge`; HEAD and origin are unchanged, the original lineage is not merged, no merge state is left, the warning names the rewrite and says re-clone. Fails before the fix (the union merge succeeds).
- Stale clone + push-retry: the stale clone commits a new event and pushes; the non-fast-forward recovery merge is refused, origin keeps the rewritten tree without the dropped file, and `store fsck` reports DIVERGED. Fails before the fix (the dropped file is republished).
- Control, ordinary concurrency: two clones commit distinct events under the same identity, same author/committer second, and same subject on the same ticket; both `sync.reconverge` and push-retry merge succeed and include both events.
- Control, unrelated empty store and fast-forward/ahead cases keep current behaviour (existing `test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py` passes unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The root cause is recorded on this ticket from git evidence: a history rewrite that did not stamp a new store epoch, re-merged from a stale clone through `sync._union_merge`.
- [ ] `compat.store_epoch_merge_target()` refuses a merge whose local-only and remote-only commits contain a rewrite copy (identical author/committer identity, both timestamps, subject, and non-empty changed-path set), and fails closed when that check cannot run.
- [ ] A sandbox test shows a stale pre-rewrite clone's `sync.reconverge` is refused with a diagnostic naming the rewrite and saying re-clone; it fails on the pre-fix code.
- [ ] A sandbox test shows a stale pre-rewrite clone's push-retry recovery merge is refused and the sandbox origin does not regain the dropped file; it fails on the pre-fix code.
- [ ] A sandbox test shows ordinary concurrent writers with identical identity, timestamps, and subject still merge through both sync and push-retry.
- [ ] `tests/integration/test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py` passes unchanged.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0 with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH; no `src/rebar` file exceeds 800 lines and the complexity ratchet reports no new or increased entries.
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` documents the rewrite-copy refusal and that a deliberate rewrite must still stamp a new epoch.
- [ ] The change lands on `main` through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
fields.title: Rewrite without new store epoch re-merges stale lineage
